NCAD Canvas Design Fundamentals I Assignment 1: Gestalt Composition Study

Assignment 1: Gestalt Composition Study

Due: Sunday 24 May, 23:59 Points: 40 Submission: PDF upload Group: Individual

Overview

This assignment asks you to demonstrate your understanding of the Gestalt principles of visual perception by creating a composition that intentionally exploits at least four of the six principles covered in Week 1: proximity, similarity, continuity, closure, figure–ground, and prägnanz (simplicity).

Your work should be developed in Adobe Illustrator or Figma and submitted as a single A3 PDF (300 dpi, CMYK colour space). Include a one-page reflective annotation (approx. 250 words) explaining how each principle manifests in your composition and why you made specific visual decisions.

Learning Outcomes

On successful completion of this assignment, you will be able to:

  • Identify and apply Gestalt principles in original visual work.
  • Articulate design decisions using appropriate critical vocabulary.
  • Produce print-ready artwork to professional technical specifications.
  • Evaluate the perceptual impact of compositional choices.

Task Breakdown

Part A — Research (10 pts)

Select one historical or contemporary designer whose work demonstrates strong application of Gestalt principles. Suitable references include Josef Müller-Brockmann, Paula Scher, Neville Brody, or Aoife Doyle. Write a short contextual note (150 words) situating their approach and identifying which principles they employ most prominently.

Part B — Composition (20 pts)

Produce a single-page abstract or semi-abstract composition, A3 landscape. The composition must be non-representational — avoid recognisable figures, objects, or letterforms. Use a restricted palette of no more than three spot colours plus black and white.

"Design is not just what it looks like and feels like. Design is how it works." — Steve Jobs. Consider this in relation to perceptual organisation: your composition should guide the viewer's eye with intention.

Part C — Reflective Annotation (10 pts)

Annotate your final composition with numbered callouts (1–4 minimum) keyed to a written annotation that names each Gestalt principle and explains the specific visual device used to achieve it. Use correct design terminology throughout.

⚠️ Submission checklist: A3 PDF at 300 dpi · CMYK colour profile · Named StudentID_Gestalt_Final.pdf · Uploaded before 23:59 on the due date. Late submissions will incur a 10% penalty per 24 hours.

NCAD Canvas Design Fundamentals I Discussion: Contemporary Irish Typography

Discussion: Contemporary Irish Typography

Posted by Aoife Brennan (Lecturer) · 14 May 2026 · 3 replies

Irish graphic design has experienced a significant renewal over the past decade, with a growing number of practitioners exploring the intersection of vernacular lettering traditions and contemporary digital practice. Studios such as Atelier David Smith, Unthink, and Provisional have produced work that consciously references the material culture of Irish signage, shopfront lettering, and Celtic manuscript traditions — while remaining formally rigorous and commercially viable.

For this discussion, I'd like you to identify one contemporary Irish designer or design studio whose typographic work you find compelling. You should:

  • Name the designer/studio and provide a brief background (2–3 sentences)
  • Share a specific example of their typographic work (include an image link or URL if possible)
  • Explain what visual or conceptual qualities make this work distinctive
  • Respond substantively to at least one peer's post

Please post your initial contribution by Wednesday 20 May and your peer response by Friday 22 May. The quality of your reasoning matters more than the volume — write with precision.
